name: Air Fryer Maple-Soy Salmon with Rice and Broccoli

components.name: Maple-Soy Salmon

ingredients.name: Raw skinless salmon, four fillets of 170 g
Neutral oil for air fryer basket

steps: Pat salmon dry and cut into four 170 g pieces. Stir maple syrup, soy sauce, sriracha and garlic until combined.
Refrigerate salmon in the maple mixture for 15-20 minutes, then remove and shake off excess glaze. Keep the remaining marinade in a separate saucepan for cooking, not for cold serving.
Air fry the salmon at 200 C in one layer for about 7-10 minutes, longer if thick, until the centre reaches 63 C. Cook in batches if needed.
Bring the reserved raw-fish-contact marinade to a full boil, then simmer until slightly syrupy. Steam broccoli until tender and toss with olive oil.

Divide rice and broccoli into four containers and add one salmon fillet and a measured share of the fully boiled glaze to each. Refrigerate promptly; eat fish early in week or freeze immediately for later use.

components.name: Jasmine Rice & Broccoli
steps: Rinse dry rice and cook in the 440 ml water using a covered saucepan; rest covered for 10 minutes after cooking.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
